candidate_relations.label: Pituitary Macroadenoma, nonfunctioning
candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is sellar cavernous hemangioma, a vascular malformation. Although the clinical presentation (large sellar/suprasellar mass, cavernous sinus invasion, visual field defect, central hypothyroidism) superficially resembles a nonfunctioning pituitary macroadenoma—and the referral presumption was macroadenoma—the imaging features (slightly hyperdense on noncontrast CT, heterogeneous T1/T2 signal, small DWI restriction foci, mild patchy enhancement, bony remodeling of clivus) are more consistent with a cavernous hemangioma. C001 asserts a different and incompatible specific entity (pituitary adenoma vs. vascular malformation), making it a conflicting subtype rather than a partial or equivalent match.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Pituitary macroadenoma is a distinct neoplastic entity from sellar cavernous hemangioma; both occupy the sellar/suprasellar region but differ in etiology, histology, and imaging characteristics

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis of sellar cavernous hemangioma is a rare entity; the clinical referral presumption of pituitary macroadenoma is explicitly noted as incorrect, supporting the conflicting classification of C001

Imaging features (hyperdensity on CT, patchy enhancement, clivus remodeling) are atypical for pituitary adenoma and more consistent with cavernous hemangioma, reinforcing high confidence in the conflicting classification
